goal: Make confirmed heavy hits easier to recognize and more distinct from glancing hits without changing damage, collision, input acceptance, or player recovery.

baseline.capture: Frame-stepped gameplay capture synchronized with input, damage-event, animation-contact, and effect-start debug markers.
observations: Damage is applied at the intended collision event.
The target recoil pose begins after the contact frame is visible.
Heavy and glancing hits use nearly identical visual and audio priorities.

response_chain.evidence: The capture begins with the heavy-attack binding held through the documented charge state.
The input-read debug marker is present in the synchronized capture.
The attack enters the committed state and the collision event resolves once.
Damage and hit classification are logged at the trusted collision event.
Contact pose, target recoil, and camera response are visible in frame stepping.
Impact sprite, audio event, and controller haptic events are captured by channel.

response_chain.owner: combat state machine and presentation cleanup
response_chain.evidence: Input acceptance, camera offset, transient scale, audio, and haptic state are checked after interruption and normal finish.

primary_hypothesis.problem: The heavy hit uses the same channel hierarchy as a glancing hit, so the trusted damage difference is not clearly represented.
primary_hypothesis.change: Give the existing heavy-hit event a distinct contact pose and target recoil onset while keeping damage, collision, attack state, recovery, and input rules unchanged.
primary_hypothesis.expected_signal: Players identify the heavy hit from matched silent and normal captures and can name the contact difference without relying only on damage text.
primary_hypothesis.falsifier: The variant remains indistinguishable, obscures the target, or is perceived as stronger only because its audio or camera channel dominates.
primary_hypothesis.competing_explanation: The weak feeling may come from attack startup or camera framing rather than impact recognition.

event_channels.necessary_information: The attack connected as the heavy classification.
event_channels.accessibility_alternative: With motion or haptics reduced, preserve a stable impact shape, distinct audio where enabled, and a non-color-only heavy-hit marker.

event_channels.necessary_information: The attack connected but did not qualify as heavy.
event_channels.accessibility_alternative: Use a distinct shape and label pattern rather than color alone.

safety.simulation_truth: Damage, collision, scoring, cooldown, hit classification, and authoritative transforms remain unchanged.
safety.input_policy: The change does not add input lock or alter buffering, cancel, or recovery rules.
safety.return_to_rest: Camera, pose overlays, transient scale, particles, audio, and haptics are restored on normal finish, interruption, pause, object reuse, and scene exit.
safety.multiplayer_authority: Not applicable to this offline capture; a networked port requires a separate authority review.

settings.behavior: Off and reduced settings leave the gameplay camera stable while preserving the impact marker and permitted audio/haptic channels.
settings.persistence: Use the product settings persistence contract.

settings.behavior: Off removes the haptic event without removing visual or audio confirmation.
settings.persistence: Use the product settings persistence contract.

accessibility.redundant_signals: Heavy and glancing classifications remain distinguishable without color, camera motion, haptics, or audio as the sole channel.

comparison.control: Current branch with the existing heavy-hit presentation.
comparison.variant: Same build and encounter with only the contact pose and target recoil onset changed.
matched_conditions: same damage, collision, cooldown, and recovery
comparison.repetition_basis: Repeat normal, interrupted, paused, and reduced-feedback paths until cleanup and classification are consistent across the supported target inputs.
acceptance: The heavy hit is distinguishable from the glancing hit through more than one permitted channel.
Trusted gameplay state and input policy match the control.
Every transient channel restores its documented rest state.
Reduced-motion and haptic-off paths preserve the hit classification.

performance.budgets: Use the combat scene's project-owned frame-time, memory, audio-voice, particle, and haptic budgets.
performance.basis: Capture on the supported target devices and compare against the same encounter control.
performance.measurement: Record frame pacing, effect lifetime, object reuse, and channel counts with the project's profilers.

decisions.decision: Test impact recognition before changing attack startup or damage.
decisions.basis: Trusted contact and damage timing are correct, while heavy and glancing feedback are not clearly differentiated.

route_out.reason: The controlled variant is defined; concrete effect work should use the engine animation, VFX, audio, and accessibility owners.
